topics.topic: Configuration-path validation order and refusal precedence for overlapping failures
questions: In what order are argument count, absolute-path, no-component, component-open, final-file metadata and file-read checks performed, especially since an empty path is both non-absolute and named as a no-component path?
What exact startup refusal and first-failure precedence apply to these cases, especially since an empty path is also non-absolute and `/` may also fail the regular-file check?

quotes:
`capability:installation.load_installation`: the command line holds
   exactly one argument, the configuration file's path, and it is absolute;
   the file is a regular private
   file of the kernel's user, one JSON object of the installation's fields; no
   service twice among the selected instances or the credentials; every
   credential header name an HTTP field-name token and every secret file
   reference an absolute path; tokens at least 43 characters and pairwise
   distinct; agent names pairwise distinct — in that order, the first failing
   one named (A16 rule 1, A17 rule 1, M28).

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not an absolute path; it cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each component with os.O_NOFOLLOW, whose presence is never tested, each directory on the way also with os.O_PATH and os.O_DIRECTORY and the file itself also with os.O_NONBLOCK (A17), the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name. The ownership, mode and regular-file checks and the read MUST all use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

The configuration file path, absolute, the process's one command-line argument (A17 rule 1); a command line without exactly one argument stops the start like a failing check of `public_op:installation.load_installation`.
load_installation: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns the loaded Installation; a failed check propagates InstallationRejectedError and nothing is kept.
judgement.why: The later flow, API, and notes fix argument-count precedence, then absolute-path validation, component opening, final-file metadata, and reading, with the first failure reported as InstallationRejectedError.

topics.topic: Required handling of potentially blocking non-regular final components
questions: What behavior is required for a non-regular final component whose Linux open operation can still block or have device-specific behavior despite `O_NONBLOCK`, since the file cannot be checked as regular until after it has been opened?

Is the kernel required to guarantee that opening every possible non-regular Linux file cannot block, even though `O_NONBLOCK` does not provide that guarantee for every file type, or is this only a best-effort rule followed by a regular-file check?

judgement.why: P2 asks the same question about whether O_NONBLOCK must guarantee nonblocking behavior for every non-regular final component or merely precede the regular-file check.

precedent.topic: Whether final-component O_NONBLOCK plus a regular-file check suffices, or opening any non-regular file must be guaranteed not to block or activate it
quotes:
A17 rule 1 (and through "here and in rule 2" the secret files) opens
      each component with `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose presence no code tests; the
      configuration path must be absolute or the start is refused (as the
      secret files' paths already were), so the walk always starts at the
      root directory and no working directory is read; each directory on the way with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY`
      so that a search-only directory such as a home of mode 0711 is passed,
      `.` and `..` opened as named and empty components skipped, a path
      naming no component unreadable, the last component opened with
      `O_NONBLOCK` so that a FIFO is refused rather than waited on, and no
      such descriptor inherited by a process the kernel starts; any
      component that cannot be opened so makes the file unreadable (State 2
      rounds 129–132, State 5 rounds 145–147).

Left open on purpose (owner, 2026-10-18). State 2 round 134 asked
      which Linux release or documentation fixes "acts as Linux documents
      it", and what a device file that blocks even under `O_NONBLOCK` at the
      configuration path does. No version is named, by the owner's
      decision; a device there can be placed only by whoever already rules
      the host. Neither is answered here, and a later round that asks again
      is answered by this paragraph.
precedent.why: State 6 specifies the O_NONBLOCK procedure and records the owner's deliberate decision not to require defined behavior for a device that can still block.

topics.topic: Descriptor lifetime and whether component walks may be cached
questions: When are the root, intermediate-directory and final-file descriptors closed, and must every configuration read and credential resolution perform a fresh component walk rather than retaining or caching any of them?

topics.topic: Precedence of A17 startup checks relative to other startup checks
questions: Where do these new A17 startup checks fall relative to the startup checks in A03, A16, A18 and A20 when more than one would fail, and which failure is reported?
